Today the Epic initialization creates an agent that writes PRDs sometiems, then the PRDs get executed from independent sessions. What would be the change to get these session to subsession more close to eachother without violating the Scheduler role of metering sub-sessions effeceively

**Current state (confirmed in code):** Epic session (architect) mints its own `claudeSessionId` via `--session-id`/`--resume` (chatRunner.cjs:533-537). PRD jobs are deliberately isolated — `scheduler.cjs` spawns `claude -p` with a **fresh** `--session-id` (scheduler.cjs:2240/2590), and PRD_AUTHORING.md explicitly documents this as intentional: "the PRD body MUST be self-contained — `claude -p` runs it on a fresh Sonnet session with NO conversation context" (scheduler.cjs:2399).

**Key finding:** the Scheduler's metering role (`sessionSlots.cjs`) is a pure process-count gate — "may one more `claude -p` launch right now?" — completely agnostic to whose session identity is being resumed. It doesn't care if a job is `--session-id <fresh>` or `--resume <existing>`. So changing session lineage for PRD jobs doesn't touch metering at all; those are genuinely orthogonal today.

**Two directions, given that:**

- **A — literal shared session** (`--resume <epicSessionId>` for PRD jobs): real continuity, but forces PRDs of one Epic to run serially (can't `--resume` the same session id concurrently), needs a new mutual-exclusion lock against the Epic's own interactive Chat/Terminal attachment (extends the existing "mutually exclusive view attachment" invariant to a third consumer), and pollutes one transcript with both architect discussion and dev-lead tool-call noise — undermining the "self-contained PRD, judged on its own AC" design that PRD_AUTHORING.md's stuck-job postmortems (fizzpop, etch-engine) actually lean on.

- **B — richer linkage, same isolation** (recommended): keep PRD jobs on fresh, independent, parallelizable sessions, but stop treating the PRD file as the *only* thing dev-lead sees. Derive a condensed context digest from the Epic session's transcript (same AIM-framework spirit as `composeEpicIntake`/`summarizeGroundingBoard`) and prepend it to the PRD's opening prompt, and record provenance (`sourceSessionId`/turn-range) on the PRD so it's inspectable. ## System — `~/.claude/` (home dir, machine-wide, every session)

## Schema consistency

**No runtime schema exists for the `PromptSession` record itself, at any layer.**

- `PromptSession` (`src/renderer/state/promptSessions.ts:29-76`) is a TS-only interface — compile-time, erased at runtime. Data read back from disk is `as`-cast, not parsed.
- The IPC boundary (`ipcSchemas.cjs:217-248`, `promptSessionsMergeActiveIndex`) validates the **envelope** only — id charset/length, map size caps, prototype-pollution guard — but each session value is `z.unknown()`. `status`'s 3-value union, `tag`'s enum, `createdAt` format: none of it is checked on the wire.
- Worse: **two independent code paths hand-construct the same record.** The renderer's New Epic flow (`promptSessions.ts:352-379`, `createPromptSession`) builds a `PromptSession` object literal directly and never touches `ensureEpic`. The CLI/scheduler path (`epicMint.cjs:216-351`, `ensureEpic`) builds a *different* object literal, with its own id scheme (`psess-<ts>-<seq>` vs `<slug>-<uuid8>`). They're kept in sync today by a doc comment ("stay shape-compatible so `hydrate()` reading a main-written index round-trips it") — convention, not enforcement.
- `ensureEpic` does enforce one real invariant well: the born-`proposed` law is fail-closed (throws if a mint call passes any status but `proposed`, `epicMint.cjs:299-305`) — so *lifecycle* is actually protected. It's field *shape* that isn't.
- Schema evolution so far = "make the new field optional and tolerate its absence" (`durableTurns`, `promptSessions.ts:85-91`) — never a real migration pass. `prdMigration.cjs` is a precedent for what a real one would look like; nothing equivalent exists for Epic records.

**Net risk:** a future field added to one constructor and not the other silently drifts — no test, no schema, no IPC check would catch it. It'd surface as a blank UI cell or a `hydrate()` crash on read, not at write time.

- `active-index.json` is **one flat, unsharded JSON file per project**, read-modify-written whole …

## The Epic (`PromptSession`) JSON schema

As-built in `src/main/lib/promptSessionSchema.cjs` — a zod schema mirroring the TS `PromptSession` interface (`src/renderer/state/promptSessions.ts:29-76`) field-for-field, and now the single validated source of truth for every Epic `ensureEpic` mints (checked right before every disk write, `epicMint.cjs:342`):

```js
PromptSessionSchema = {
  id: string,                          // required
  cwd: string,                         // required
  goalText: string,                    // required
  claudeSessionId: string,             // required
  status: 'proposed' | 'active' | 'completed',  // required
  createdAt: string,                   // required
  completedAt: string | null,          // required
  resumedFromId?: string | null,       // optional
  tag?: EpicTagSchema,                 // optional
  openingPrompt?: string | null,       // optional
  source?: EpicSourceSchema,           // optional
  agentType?: string,                  // optional
}

EpicTagSchema = enum:
  'feature' | 'bug' | 'discussion' | 'build' |
  'project-home-builder' | 'bilko-host-publisher'

EpicSourceSchema = {
  producer: 'rca-hook' | 'feedback-sweep' | 'propose-epic' | 'scheduler-dispatch',  // required
  prdSlug?: string,
  runId?: string,
  sourceTabId?: string,
}
```

PRD to EPIC Communication

This seems to be broken. I do not understand how does the PRDs check back in with the Agent that started them so that, that agent can move on?

It's broken, and I found the exact defect. Here's how it's *supposed* to work, then why it doesn't.

## The intended mechanism

There's no polling and no agent-to-agent call. It's a one-way write into the Epic's event chain:

1. A PRD file carries `sourcePromptId: <epic-id>` in its frontmatter (and the queue row carries `epicId`).
2. When a job hits a terminal status, `scheduler.cjs:3057` fires `notifyOriginatingTab(job)`.
3. That reads the PRD's frontmatter to get `sourcePromptId`, then calls `appendResponseEventIfKnown` (`src/main/promptSessionEvents.cjs:55`), which appends a `response` event onto that Epic's chain in `active-index.json` and broadcasts `promptSession:event-appended` to the renderer.
4. The Epic's conversation shows it as a new message. The agent "moves on" because the result lands in its session as an inbound turn — not because it waited.

## Why it never fires

`notifyOriginatingTab` locates the PRD via `prdPathForJob(job)` → `resolvePrdWriteDir(cwd)` → `<cwd>/session-manager-operations/scheduler/prds/<slug>.md` — **the retired flat directory**. Every modern PRD lives in `scheduler/epics/<epicId>/prds/`. That dir contains only zero-byte `.reserved-NNN` stubs, no `.md` files at all.

Compounding it: `archiveCompletedPrd` renames the file into `prds-archived/` at line 3052-3054, *immediately before* the notify at 3057. So even with correct dir resolution, the live path would be gone.

`parsePrdRaw` ENOENTs → `prd = null` → `sourcePromptId` null → both the transcript append and the response-event append are skipped → it silently falls through to a cwd-matched open tab and fires an unrelated `chat:external-send`.

**Reproduced on your own data:** PRDs 961/962/963/964 (Epic `psess-msckxplj-24`) and 967 (`psess-msch6x36-16`) all completed between 02:22 and 03:16 today. The newest event on either Epic's chain predates every one of those completions. Zero response events landed.

**The tell that confirms it:** `notifyNeedsReview` (line 1920) has a `job.e…

## The traffic light

Three states, matched to what the Architect must actually *do*:

| Colour | Job status | Meaning | Architect action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🟢 sage | `completed` | checked in clean | none |
| 🟡 butter | `needs_review` | checked in **asking a question** | decide — this is the main "act" state |
| 🔴 accent | `failed` | checked in broken | re-scope or re-queue |
| neutral / pulse | `pending` / `running` | hasn't checked in yet | wait |

No new palette. All three tones already exist in `sched-primitives.tsx:212` (`STATUS_TONE`) and `epic-primitives.tsx:11` — the app just wasn't using them on these surfaces.

## The contract, inverted

A check-in currently *asserts* an outcome. It now *requests* one:

> PRD `<slug>` reports `completed`. **This is an unverified claim.** Read `<abs path>`, check each acceptance criterion against the actual working tree, reply VERIFIED or REFUTED with per-criterion evidence.

The job's status becomes an input to the Epic's judgment, never a substitute for it.

**986 `checkin-triggers-epic-validation`** — on a successful check-in, the scheduler enqueues exactly one validation prompt into the authoring Epic's session via `enqueueExternalPrompt(epicId, prompt)` (`chatRunner.cjs:821`, already routes to Epic ids). The event is born `validation: 'unvalidated'` — never `'verified'` — regardless of what the job claims.

The prompt names the exact trap that produced this: exit code 0, a green queue row, and a confident completion report are **not evidence** — only the working tree is. It's instructed to run `git diff --stat` for the run window and treat an empty diff on an implementation PRD as REFUTED. That single rule would have caught 972 in seconds.

Four gates, all mandatory: active Epics only, once per `(epicId, prdSlug)`, inside the ≤3 session-slot pool, and a kill-switch env var. Plus a loop guard with its own test so a validation reply can't trigger another validation. The slot-pool gate isn't ceremony — a prompt per check-in is exactly the fan-out shape that OOM-killed Electron on 2026-06-10.

**987 `traffic-light-reads-epic-verdict`** — retargets all three indicators (974's chip, 975's row rollup, 976's response line) off the job's claim and onto the Epic's verdict. New neutral **claimed** tone for `unvalidated`. The load-bearing line, which I made its own named test: *a job with `outcome: completed` and `validation: unvalidated` renders claimed, never green.* And `refuted` ranks **above** `failed` in the Epic-row prec…

PRD 832 changed `parallelGroup` to be **unique per PRD** and moved ordering to `dependsOn`. `prdCreate.cjs:173` even warns that an explicit `parallelGroup` is *"deprecated and ignored — numbers are unique per project"*.

But `schedulerBatch.cjs` was never updated. It still treats `parallelGroup` as a **wave number**:

- `pickForProject` computes `lowestPendingGroup`, then filters the batch to **only jobs in that one group** (`schedulerBatch.cjs:156,171,188`). Unique numbers ⇒ every group is a singleton ⇒ **batch size is always 1**.
- Worse, the running-gate at `schedulerBatch.cjs:141-145`: if any lower group is in flight, every higher group is **held**. Since numbers are monotonically allocated upward, new PRDs always sit above the running one — so the queue is fully serialized on top of that.
- The `late-arrival` escape hatch (line 147, fires in parallel when `lowestPendingGroup < lowestActive`) is unreachable in practice for the same monotonic-allocation reason.

Simulated against your live queue with 5 free slots and nothing running:

```
pickNextBatch(idle jobs, cap 5) → ["979-fix-transcript-paged-reads"]   // 1 job
```

Meanwhile `dependsOn` says **4 jobs are eligible right now**:

```
985-notify-epic-prd-path-fix-redo   ELIGIBLE
984-context-digest-prd-focus-guard  ELIGIBLE
983-verdict-downgrade-must-stick    ELIGIBLE

987 / 986 / 982 / 981               BLOCKED (real, correct chains)
```

So your PRD wiring is fine — `dependsOn` is doing exactly the right thing, gating 4 and freeing 4. The group gate then throws that away and picks one.
